title: Route-invocation wide-table with sparse indexing & late-arrival reconciliation
creator: Aisha Romero
description:
Problem: multiple Console telemetry sources (route events, model invocation logs, KV-cache hits, kernel profile metrics) are split across event streams with differing arrival times and granularities. Analysts and SREs need a single, queryable wide-table at the route-invocation grain for fast ad-hoc queries, small-scale ML experiments, and accurate per-request cost/latency attribution. Current denorm attempts are either too large (full denormalized event store) or too lossy (pre-aggregated rollups).

Goal: produce a curated, storage-efficient 'route_invocation_wide' canonical table with: 1) stable primary key (invocation_id), 2) robust handling of late-arriving events (upserts with reconciliation window), 3) sparse indexing for high-cardinality dimensions (model_variant, kernel_profile, tenant_tag), and 4) materialized incremental views for common SLA and cost queries. The table should support fast joins with Console route metadata and be inexpensive to query for exploratory analysis.

Design highlights:
- Grain: one row per invocation_id (generated client-side or assigned by ingestion). Backfill strategy for sessions missing invocation_id will de-dupe on (workspace_id, route_id, start_ts, user_agent_hash).
- Column set (initial): invocation_id, workspace_id, route_id, route_version, model_family, model_variant, kernel_profile, sequence_length, token_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, inference_latency_ms, serve_region, host_pool, user_cohort_tag, request_timestamp, ingestion_timestamp, raw_event_payload_path, dedup_hash, row_status (complete|partial|reconciled).
- Partitioning: time-based partitioning on request_timestamp (weekly) and clustering by workspace_id, route_id for common filters.
- Sparse indexing: build Bloom-filter-like index structures or use sparse materialized indexes on model_variant and kernel_profile to keep index size proportional to distinct hot keys. Document expected cardinalities and eviction policy for index entries older than 90 days.
- Late-arrival reconciliation: define a reconciliation window (default 72 hours) where incoming late events trigger idempotent upserts. Outside window, late events write to a late_event_log table and schedule a prioritized backfill job. Upserts must be bounded and idempotent.
- Storage/cost controls: support TTL compaction for raw_event_payload_path after 30 days; maintain summarized rows for >180 days (daily aggregations) and prune detailed rows to reduce storage.
- Materialized views: create two MV layers: (A) invocation_slo_mv with percentile latency and error counts by route/model for the last 7/30 days; (B) route_cost_mv that joins token_count with model_unit_cost to provide per-route cost-attribution. Both MVs should be refreshable incrementally and exposed to analysts via console BigQuery/Redshift views.
- Data contracts and alerts: schema evolution requires a signed contract in Confluence and a compatibility check in CI. Add a daily data-quality job that verifies primary-key uniqueness, null-rate thresholds, and reconciliation backlog size; create PagerDuty rule for >2% reconciliation backlog growth over 24h.

Backfill plan:
1) Run a 7-day pilot ingest from ingestion-prod-raw into a shadow route_invocation_wide table with upsert semantics; compare counts and key distributions to existing sessionized facts.
2) Validate sparse index size and query performance for top 10 analyst queries.
3) If pilot passes, schedule full backfill for 90 days with throttled write rates and monitoring.

Operational runbook (summary):
- Monitor: ingestion lag, reconciliation queue length, MV refresh failures, index size growth.
- Remediation: pause upstream producers if reconciliation queue >10k for 4 hours; run dedupe/backfill job; escalate to data-platform.

Why this is unique and valuable: consolidates multi-source telemetry into a minimal, query-friendly canonical table optimized for both exploration and lightweight ML, while explicitly addressing late-arrivals and index bloat — a common pain point for Console analytics teams.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical table schema reviewed and signed off by analytics and platform engineers.
Pilot shadow table ingest validates idempotent upserts and reconciliation logic over 7 days with <0.5% unexpected duplicates.
Sparse indexing approach reduces index storage by >=50% vs naive full inverted index in pilot workload.
Two materialized views (invocation_slo_mv and route_cost_mv) exist, refresh incrementally, and return results within SLA: 5s for 95th percentile queries on last-7d partitions.
Data quality checks run nightly and alert if primary-key uniqueness or reconciliation backlog thresholds breached.
comments: 2025-01-31 - Liam: Initial spike to evaluate upsert performance on Redshift RA3 and BigQuery MERGE costs. Found BigQuery MERGE costs high for large upserts; leaning to Redshift/Materialize for upserts.
2025-02-03 - Aisha: Added sparse index experiments: prototype using partial materialized tables keyed by model_variant hash. Need SRE input on eviction policy.

2025-02-06 - Data-Platform review: Recommended reconciliation window of 72h and suggested storing raw payload path instead of full payload to reduce storage. Also requested a Confluence data contract before backfill.
